general_information.Description: - Description: Discourse Analysis (DA) is an interdisciplinary field of linguistics that explores language beyond the sentence level in both spoken and written forms, viewing it as a social practice through DA methodologies such as conversation analysis, corpus linguistics, and multimodal analysis. - Objectives: Drawing from linguistics, sociology, and communication studies, the course aims to introduce students to key theories, concepts, and practices in DA, covering a range of topics such as Identity, Gender, Culture, Ideology, Code-switching, Pragmatics, Discourse grammar, Intertextuality, and Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA). This course also emphasizes critical thinking, open-mindedness, and research skills, encouraging students to analyze various texts and communication events creatively and deeply. It helps develop students’ ability to work independently, effectively collaborate in pairs and groups and direct their own learning. Additionally, it helps enhance students' linguistic skills and language proficiency equivalent to C1 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), preparing them for careers in linguistics, communication, and education. - Teaching and Learning Methodology: This course applies instructional, communicative, and interactive discussions with guidelines for pre-lesson and post-lesson activities designed to reinforce acquired skills, opportunities to explore theoretical and practical aspects of the subject matter, an open-minded approach to addressing questions and clarifying any confusions during lessons, supplementary lectures and discussions to enhance students’ engagement with the topics, text analysis projects or group research presentations to further develop practical skills in discourse analysis, and peer review sessions to help students gain experience in giving and receiving constructive feedback.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible to do all exercises, assignments, and actitvities given by instructors in class or at home and submit on time. - Use laptops in class only for learning purposes. - Be punctual for class. - Actively participate in class discussions. - Preview and review the lessons. - Check vocabulary for comprehension. - Work with a group for group discussions and activities.
general_information.Note: On-going Assessment - 02 assignments: 20% (10% each) - 02 Progress test: 30% (15 % each) Final Exam: 50%

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Critique basic concepts and principles of discourse analysis by comparing and contrasting different perspectives on discourse analysis
Evaluate the relationship between language use and social factors such as gender, identity, and ideology in various contexts
Formulate comprehensive analyses by applying pragmatic concepts to examine how meaning is constructed and communicated across diverse social contexts
Differentiate written, spoken, and digital genres by identifying their structural features, cultural contexts, and communicative purposes
Analyze various types of texts through conversation analysis, corpus-based studies, and multimodal discourse analysis
Generate effective communication in academic and professional contexts with discourse analysis knowledge
Construct knowledge in linguistic areas by evaluating online resources and establishing ethical considerations related to gender, ideology, and culture
Develop professionalism and respect with other members in class activities, discussions, and group work
